subject: Post-call: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finlytics.ai>, Finlytics Procurement <procurement@finlytics.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider

Hi Alex / team 	6

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap on the questions we discussed around end-to-end performance and next steps to validate p95/p99 targets with Redwood hosted API vs your current provider:

Summary of what I heard:
- Your primary SLO target for interactive features is p95 <= 350ms and p99 <= 700ms end-to-end (including network + model streaming).
- Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent users for the feature initially, expected to scale to ~800 over 12 months.
- Expected steady-state RPS (per instance of the feature): ~70 req/s; average tokens per response ~220 tokens.
- Streaming is critical for perceived latency (token-by-token streaming), not just final response time.
- You currently see provider p95 ~350ms, p99 ~700ms for short prompts; spikes during bursts are the main concern.

What we can do / proposed next steps:
1) Redwood will run a comparative bench (48-hour window) that mimics your traffic profile (concurrency, RPS, token distribution, streaming). This will measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99 for both streaming and non-streaming paths.
2) Please share the sample traffic CSV (requests/sec, concurrency bins, tokens distribution) and a representative prompt set. I attached a CSV template (finlytics-test-plan.csv) you can fill.
3) We'll set up a sandbox API key and test harness (link below) and provide access to a dashboard with latency percentiles per route.
4) For procurement: if you want a Dedicated or Private evaluation, we can scope cost estimates after the bench. For hosted, we can run the bench in our hosted environment.

Attached: redwood_slo_matrix_v1.pdf (shows how we measure p95/p99 including network and streaming), plus the finlytics test plan template.

Can you confirm the traffic profile and whether you want the bench to include the same model version you currently use (you mentioned "gpt-small-v2") or try Redwood-optimized variants?

Happy to jump on a quick 20-min call to kick off the bench.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0123

Hi Laura 	6

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers you quoted are accurate to our observations. A few clarifications from our side:
- Our current provider reports p95 ~350ms and p99 ~700ms for the short prompt set we tested; however, we see p99 blow up to 1.2s during bursty traffic (spike events).
- Concurrency here refers to concurrent active sessions (token-streaming open connections). Typical session length is ~4	66 seconds for these prompts.
- We do rely on streaming in the product; perceived latency is effectively token arrival rate rather than final completion time.

I've attached a filled-first-pass of the test-plan (see attachment). We'll follow up with a CSV export of historical traffic by EOD tomorrow.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood's bench emulate the open-connection streaming behavior and measure token-latency percentiles (time-to-first-token, token inter-arrival)?
2) Can you include an apples-to-apples comparison against our current provider using the same model version (gpt-small-v2)?

If those are yes, please go ahead and provision the sandbox and send the test access. Procurement will need an SOW and a temporary evaluation agreement (we'll coordinate with procurement).

Appreciate it 	6
Alex
Product Lead, Finlytics
alex.johnson@finlytics.ai

Alex 	6

Yes to both asks. A couple notes on methodology so expectations are aligned:
- We'll run two parallel streams: (A) hosted Redwood API with the same model binary you use where possible, and (B) your current provider (you can provide access or we can replay recorded responses if direct access isn't possible).
- Bench will capture: time-to-first-token, p50/p95/p99 of first-token and full-completion, token inter-arrival percentiles, and concurrency impact across bins (1	650, 51	6200, 201+).
- We'll include packet-level network variation in the hosted run to mimic your geographic mix (US east/west).
- If streaming is implemented as chunked HTTP events in your app, we'll mirror that so the token inter-arrival measurements are apples-to-apples.

Proposed schedule:
- 8/19: we start sandbox + bench provisioning (sandbox creds + dashboard link sent).
- 8/20	6/8/21: 48-hour bench run (we'll run steady-state + two burst windows).
- 8/24: deliver bench report + latency plots and follow-up call to go over regressions/recommendations.

I'll start provisioning the sandbox today. Aditya, can you scope the bench (instances, model variants to test) and confirm whether we need a Dedicated eval or hosted will suffice for initial measurement?

Alex & procurement 	6 I'll drop the SOW and evaluation agreement templates to procurement after this thread.

Best,
Laura
